prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: I keep B016 as my final position, as a single-part prize. The case rests on a closed chain from symmetry argument to measurement: Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal-invariant band insulators fall into a Z2 classification with protected helical edge states, and Molenkamp's group then observed edge transport consistent with that picture in HgTe quantum wells in 2007. The result established topology as a general organizing principle for band structure with spin-orbit coupling, and it has been tested across several material platforms for almost two decades. Nobody in round 1 argued that it is premature, and the chair's summary records that members on both sides regard it as mature and reproduced. On the chair's question of which criterion should decide between B014 and B016, I weigh conceptual reach and a decisive prediction-and-observation loop most heavily, and I treat clean attribution as a constraint to be satisfied rather than as a tie-breaker that outranks the science. I would be uncomfortable if a clean two-name allocation alone decided the question while an overlap with earlier prizes was treated as disqualifying for one candidate only. B014 faces the same kind of overlap argument, against 2005 and 2012, that B016 faces against 2016.
statement.case_against: After round 1 I think the attribution problem is the real weakness and I have not talked myself out of it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the platform and their paper preceded the observation, Zhang cannot be a laureate, and the three-dimensional work of Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and Hasan lies outside the candidate. A three-name prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is defensible on the narrow citation (prediction of the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its first observation), but it leaves a visible gap, and Johansson and Mehlig are right that edge conductance in HgTe has been less ideal than the early picture suggested. Because the three-person ceiling is already used, I cannot repair the gap by adding names. The 2016 prize is a further risk: I read it as covering topological phase transitions and Chern-type states with broken time-reversal symmetry, not Z2 insulators, but a committee that reads it more broadly would reasonably prefer B014. B014 has the broadest opening support and the cleaner credit, and I regard it as a legitimate winner, not a lesser option.

responses.point: Kroll argues that B014 has the broadest support (no member ranks it below fourth), is a single well-defined invention with magic-wavelength trapping, and has the cleanest two-name attribution with no obvious person missing from the core.
responses.response: I accept the attribution point and the breadth of support, and I think the lattice clock is a real invention and not just an application of the comb. My disagreement is about what to do with breadth of support. A candidate that nobody ranks below fourth can also be one nobody feels strongly about, and the committee has been told not to treat counts as a substitute for judgement. On substance, I find the magic-wavelength idea less of a change in how we understand nature than a Z2 classification of insulating states. I also note your Boulder disclosure and agree with the chair that it needs resolving. That is a reason to settle it openly, not a reason to discount your scientific argument.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the lattice clock is a different invention with its own physics from the 2005 comb prize, that the concept-versus-performance split between Katori and Ye is the normal pattern for an instrument prize, and that the 2005 work only supplied the comb that links optical frequencies to counting electronics.
responses.response: That is the best defence of B014 against the overlap objection, and it moves me part of the way. If the comb is infrastructure and the lattice clock a separate principle, the 2005 overlap is smaller than I implied in round 1. The same logic must be applied to B016 against 2016, where the Z2 state is also a separate step from Haldane's Chern insulator. So the overlap argument cannot count against B016 more than against B014. Where we still differ is on weight: I read a new topological classification as having wider reach than the highest-accuracy instrument, and the SI redefinition that supports your case is still pending, whereas the topological result needs no further milestone.

responses.point: Johansson also prefers B016 but states that the credit set is incomplete, that HgTe edge quantization is imperfect in longer channels, and that B014 would be the cleaner two-person allocation if the HgTe attribution cannot be defended.
responses.response: I agree with your risk assessment and want to be exact about where I stand relative to it. I think the HgTe attribution can be defended through the citation wording: it credits the prediction of the Z2 state and its first observation, not the discovery of HgTe as a platform. The imperfect quantization is real, but the helical edge picture was subsequently seen in other materials, so the observation does not depend on HgTe alone. If a colleague convincingly shows that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal was essential rather than enabling, I would regard B014 as the better prize, which is the same condition you state.

responses.point: Olsson now supports B014 as the cleanest attribution, and treats its priority and chronology details as unverified, while she also flags a possible institutional link to Katori through Japanese exchanges that she has not yet checked.
responses.response: I take your point that clean attribution matters and that B014 fits the physics criterion of an invention. Your own caution about unverified priority among Katori, Ye and the Paris, PTB and NIST groups matters here, because a two-name prize that looks clean in the ballots could be contested once those details are checked, in the same way that the HgTe gap is contested for B016. I would ask you to resolve the Japan connection before any count and to say what it is. I do not think it requires withdrawal from the discussion unless it turns out to be a direct tie to Katori.

responses.point: The chair moved from B021 to B014 because it combines the criteria best and warns that this may reflect a wish not to over-promote his own field, and asks in the summary what would move members between B014 and B016.
responses.response: I appreciate the candour about your move. In answer to your question, I would move to B014 if (a) the committee judges that the 2016 prize already covers Z2 topological insulators, or (b) the HgTe credit gap is shown to be unfair to a living person who can be named within a three-person ceiling, or (c) the committee decides that attribution clarity must come first. None of these has been established in round 1. I note that B021 remains on my alternatives, but I do not see a credit rationale for IceCube any stronger than you do, so I leave that alternative as a lower-ranked fallback.

responses.point: Mehlig moved to B016 as his preferred outcome, arguing that Z2 time-reversal-invariant insulators and their helical edge states are distinct from the 2016 prize, and that HgTe edge quantization weakens the experimental half of the story.
responses.response: I agree that the Z2 insulators are distinct from the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz subject matter, and your account of the 2016 prize supports my reading. Where I would push back slightly is on the experimental half: the HgTe result was a clear observation of nonlocal edge transport, and reproduction elsewhere supports the effect even if the quantization is less ideal than predicted. I also share your caution about the gap with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. We should not claim more certainty than we have about chronology, since we are both working from recollection and not from the nomination files.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as essential to the HgTe observation, which would make a three-name B016 prize unfair and favour B014.
Whether the 2016 prize is read as covering Z2 topological insulators; I believe it does not, but I cannot establish that against the committee as a whole.

Whether my preference for conceptual reach over clean attribution is a sound criterion or a bias from my theoretical background, since I am more at ease with a symmetry-and-classification argument than with a precision-measurement one.
I rely on recollection for priority and chronology in HgTe and in the lattice-clock work, and have not checked these against the nomination files.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any credited name on B016, B014 or B021 is apparent from my profile. My PhD supervisor David Gross and frequent co-author Thomas Van Riet have no connection to those candidates that I know of. My research in string theory, quantum gravity and cosmology is closest to B001, which I am not proposing. I note the field proximity and do not treat it as a recusal issue. I have no update from round 1, and I have no private knowledge of any other deliberation.
